name: Carolina Wren
facts: Call pattern: a ringing "teakettle-teakettle-teakettle," startlingly loud for a bird that weighs less than an ounce. One male may know dozens of song variations.
Habitat: tangled undergrowth, brush piles and garages. Will nest in flowerpots, mailboxes and old boots.
Migration: none. Pairs hold a territory all year, and hard winters knock back numbers at the northern edge of the range.
